# Draft:Copernicus Bilingual High School in Warsaw

----
| website                 = https://kopernik.edu.pl/
| image                   = XXXIII Liceum Ogólnokształcące Dwujęzyczne im. Mikołaja Kopernika w Warszawie 2017.jpg
| caption                 = School's building
}}Copernicus Bilingual High School in Warsaw – a state high school located at 76 Józefa Bema St. in Warsaw's Wola district. First in Poland to offer an International Baccalaureate class.
The school ranks high among other High Schools in Poland in Matura exam rankings as well as Science Olympiads and competitions. It offers IB's Diploma Programme as well as Middle Years Programme.
School's history
The school building at 76 Bema St., designed by Teodor Łapiński and Józef Krupa, was put into service in 1927. After the German invasion of 1939 the building was turned into a hospital. During the German occupation many teachers schooled in secret classes or were active in the underground. Throughout the World War II education took place in a barrack on Wolska St., divided between several schools.
In 1949 Children Friends Association's school No. IV was established with Henryk Gronkowski as the headmaster and Włodzimierz Lamparski taking his place in 1952. Year later the first class graduated, ranking the school among the best in the country. Between 1957 and 1959 the building housed both the High School (now No. XXXIII) as well as a Primary School. Genowefa Liponoga was the head at that time.
In 1959 Jan Dobrowolski became the principal. A year after that, the school was named after Nicolaus Copernicus. The school became the first one in post-war Poland to open a class with English as the language of instruction in 1962. On October 21st 1970 a ceremonial inauguration was held, celebrating the 500th anniversary of Copernicus' birth.
After 20 years of managing the school, Jan Dobrowolski retired and Albert Stoma became the new principal. The school employed the first non-Polish native speaker as a teacher in 1984. In September 1993, along Polish Navy High School in Gdynia, Copernicus High School became the first school in Poland to have an International Baccalaureate class with English as the language of instruction. Albert Stoma retired in 2010, and Justyna Matejczyk became the new principal.
Since September 2012 up until 2017, when Junior High's were terminated in Poland, together with the Władysław Sikorski Bilingual Junior High Copernicus Highschool establishment a School Complex No. 117
The list of principals
* 1949–1951 – Henryk Gronkowski
* 1952–1957 – Włodzimierz Lamparski
* 1957–1959 – Genowefa Liponoga
* 1959–1979 – Jan Dobrowolski
* 1979–2010 – Albert Stoma
* od 2010 – Justyna Rosiek (Matejczyk)
